regime_assessment.summary: Arc launch-day speculative secondary trading remains material and leadership is concentrating in ARGUS and TOLLY, but deeper structural review fails the hard-gate standard for both candidates. The ecosystem-level regime therefore remains worth tracking while token-level paper entry remains blocked.
regime_assessment.rwa_note: BUIDL and USYC are available on Arc for trading/lending/collateral, but no Arc-specific secondary-volume or collateral-utilization evidence was strong enough in this run to count RWA availability as actual usage.

leadership.market_evidence: ARGUS remains the leading Arc-native speculative token by observed on-chain secondary trading. OpenSea showed roughly 12.3k holders and about $29.9M one-day volume; Arc venue data showed ARGUS/USDC leading around $25M in 24h trading. Multiple CEX listings also expanded distribution.
gate_reasons: Arcscan identifies the token contract as a 45-byte proxy whose implementation source code is not verified, preventing reliable audit of upgrade authority, minting, fee mutation, transfer restrictions and other privileged controls.
Arcscan could not provide a normal holder query and noted insufficient native liquidity for its own reliable price derivation at the observed checkpoint.

A third-party automated scanner separately flagged possible hidden-mint, mutable-fee, excess-debit and trading-toggle capabilities. These flags are not treated as proven because the implementation is unverified, but the inability to resolve them reinforces rejection under the hard-gate rule.

Public documentation does not establish that all Argus platform revenue automatically accrues to ARGUS holders; therefore direct token value-capture certainty is weaker than earlier provisional reporting suggested.

leadership.market_evidence: TOLLY remains the second major Arc-native launch-day leader with roughly $10.6M observed TOLLY/USDC 24h trading and about 7.7k holders.
gate_reasons: Arcscan holder concentration remained high: top 10 about 26.45% and top 100 about 72.78% at the checkpoint.
Observed pool depth was only about $269k against roughly $10.75M on-chain market capitalization, creating poor executable-liquidity characteristics for the framework.
Arcscan reported an internal supply-accounting inconsistency in which indexed holder balances summed to more than contract-reported total supply; this requires resolution before entry.
TOLLY economics include holder-reward and fee-routing incentives, contaminating the discretionary-demand signal.

paper_portfolio.note: Existing paper holdings remain hold/no-add this run. ZEC remains the strongest recent confirmation but lacks a fresh independent selective-wallet leg for another scale-up.

why_signal_matters_now: The previous Arc alert explicitly identified ARGUS as the first structural-review target. Deeper review now resolves that uncertainty negatively: market leadership strengthened, but the token still cannot clear the non-negotiable structural gates. This is a meaningful rejection rather than a missed entry.
major_uncertainties: Arc launch-day data remain fast-moving and some analytics providers disagree on market cap, liquidity and volume.
Automated contract-security scanner flags may contain false positives and are not treated as confirmed vulnerabilities.
The degree of wash trading, bot activity and wallet independence across Arc-native launch tokens remains unresolved.
Arc RWA product availability has not yet translated into verified chain-specific secondary trading or collateral-utilization evidence in this research record.
